title: Investment Programme for Resilience - phase III
description: The Investment Programme for Resilience (IPR) is a comprehensive, inclusive, and integrated response to the needs of the most vulnerable/marginalized communities in Palestine.IPR III aims at further expanding the community infrastructure component, to strengthen the access to socio-economic services and to enhance social engagement in marginalized and disadvantaged communities, by rehabilitating/constructing/expanding small-scale needs-based infrastructure, building the capacities of the entities to manage and operate the targeted facilities, organizing social cohesion activities and throughout the project life cycle ensure the inclusion of all groups in the design, implementation and follow up of locally designed and driven initiatives.

title: Promoting Biodiversity and Ecosystem-Bases Adaptation to Climate Change in Wadi Gaza
description: The project aims to protect the rapidly deteriorating natural resources in Wadi Gaza, improve the livelihoods of the residents of the Gaza Strip, as well as strengthen the institutional capacity of the Joint Service Council of Wadi Gaza and the neighbouring municipalities. The proposed initiative will also create nature-based solutions to mitigate the flood risks and enhance the biodiversity at the Wadi, as well as provide green and safe public areas and utilities for Gaza residents, especially for vulnerable groups such as women, youth, people with disabilities (PWDs), and the elderly. The project will focus on enhancing the knowledge and capacities of the Joint Service Council of Wadi Gaza (JSC-WG) and member municipalities in the protection, maintenance, and operation of Wadi Gaza. It will also focus on strengthening social inclusion and engaging local communities in the planning, design, and implementation of all interventions in Wadi Gaza.

title: Early Recovery and Reconstruction 2024
description: Against the backdrop of the unprecedented destruction caused by the ongoing war and the humanitarian catastrophe unfolding in the Gaza Strip, this Initiation Plan enables UNDP/PAPP to provide and scale-up ongoing critical support to emergency response in Gaza. It also allows UNDP/PAPP to generate knowledge that further informs immediate responses on the ground and contributes to evidence-based early recovery planning, while leveraging UNDP’s integrator role to bring all relevant partners and stakeholders together around critical issues to enhance cohesive and integrated early recovery planning.

title: Establishment of the National 911 Emergency Call Center
description: The project entails refurbishing the basement floor of the Ministry of Interiors facility in Ramallah to house the newly established 911 Emergency Call Center. The center once operational will allow for an integrated and unified emergency response system throughout the West Bank which will reduce response times by critical emergency response teams such as ambulance crews, civil defense firefighting units, and civil police

title: Responding to the Solid Waste Management Crisis in the Gaza strip
description: The project aims to urgently address the solid waste crisis and restore solid waste management services in the Gaza Strip is of paramount importance. It represents a critical component of the ongoing humanitarian response, as well as a prerequisite for early recovery and for internally displaced people to return to their homes and rebuild their lives and livelihoods as soon as the security conditions on the ground allow so. The project was designed to enhance the operational capacities of the solid waste management service providers, ensuring more effective and efficient waste collection and transfer. It focuses on controlled disposal and proper management of solid waste disposal sites, alongside restoring capabilities for the safe segregation, collection, and treatment of medical and hazardous waste. Ultimately, these efforts will strengthen the service providers operational capacities, facilitating the restoration, scaling up and sustainability of solid waste management services.

title: Gaza Emergency Health Response
description: The ongoing war has devastated Gaza’s health sector, with over 60% of facilities destroyed or inoperable by September 2024, leaving only 17 of 36 hospitals partially functioning. Rising injuries and severe shortages of trauma and essential health supplies have overwhelmed hospitals like Al-Ahli, severely limiting life-saving care. Restricted access for emergency teams further disrupts critical services, including obstetric care, chronic disease management, and infection treatment, while waste accumulation and water contamination heighten health risks for the population.In response to the unprecedented challenges facing Gazas health system, this partnership will strengthen access to essential trauma services and enhance Al-Ahli Hospitals capacity to deliver critical healthcare. The project will be implemented in close collaboration with the Ministry of Health, WHO, and the Health Cluster, aligning with both national and international health strategies. It will focus on rehabilitating and operationalizing the ICU and operating rooms, deploying health staff, and building medical staff capacity, while also creating job opportunities for health workers and ensuring the continuity of essential health services in Gaza.

title: Gaza Recovery, Reconstruction and Development (GRRD) Planning
description: Gaza Recovery, Reconstruction and Development (GRRD) Planning-The project encompasses multiple strategic outputs, including the establishment of a technically skilled Gaza Reconstruction team to develop and oversee the GRRD Plan, fostering multi-stakeholder engagement with backstopping support from IUAV and other stakeholders to align international best practices, and conducting a on the ground damage assessment ofto inform a recovery and reconstruction efforts. Additionally, this initiative will strengthen MoPICs internal capabilities, empowering it to lead recovery coordination effectively across ministries and with international partners.By combining technical capacity building, inclusive stakeholder engagement, and extensive community assessments, this initiative reflects a cohesive, government-led vision for Gazas sustainable recovery. It emphasizes dignified living conditions, social cohesion, and robust infrastructure rebuilding to foster a stable future for all affected populations.
